findings.oracle: Replaced the identity passthrough with test_reads_full_document_with_correct_offset_and_length (content = bytes(range(256))*2; oracle = test-chosen 512-byte sequence) asserting result == content, read_call_count == 1, and read_args == [(0, 512)]; added test_partial_read_would_not_satisfy_full_content (capped-read document) asserting requested_lengths == [len(content)] and result == content[:4]. A no-op or wrong offset/length read_document_for_scan now fails (verified RED by patching read_args expectation).

Removed the conditional 'if harness.worker() is not None' guard. Now unconditionally asserts a worker is spawned, that doc.read_call_count == 0 immediately after trigger_scan (no UI-thread read), waits for completion (finished is True), asserts doc.read_call_count >= 1, asserts read_thread_ids is non-empty, that every read thread id != main thread id, and that tracemalloc peak UI-thread allocation for a real 50 MiB document stays < 1 MiB. A regression that fails to spawn the worker or reads on the UI thread now fails instead of silently no-opping.

Added TestBridgeRealSandboxLifecycle (8 tests, @pytest.mark.integration/@pytest.mark.spawns_process) driving a real SandboxBridge whose manager (_RealLocalManager) wraps the conftest LocalProcessSandbox that genuinely runs sys.executable as a subprocess and diffs its workdir. Oracle = a deterministic driver script whose payload bytes, stdout text, exit code, and dropped-file name are all test-chosen. Asserts the bridge surfaces exact stdout 'bridge-run-ok', exit_code 0/9, result success/error, the genuinely-created artefact (operation 'created', exact path, size == len(payload), on-disk sha256 match), bridge.state.binary_loaded/target_path; real copy_to->copy_from byte round-trip through the workdir; extract_iocs returning IPv4 203.0.113.50 parsed from a genuinely-observed dropped-file path (verified RED by patching the expected IP); and ToolError on missing binary, missing sandbox file, and no-report-before-run. The in-memory fixture tests remain as fast unit coverage.
